intro: You have arrived at Limyra Ancient City, in Finike, Antalya province. This Lycian city spans a long story, from the 5th century BC to the 6th century AD, and it is known for three treasures: the tomb monument of Pericles of Limyra, a Roman theatre and the Kaineus relief.
history: In Lycian inscriptions the city appears as 'Zemuri'. In the first half of the 4th century BC, under King Pericles, it became the capital of Lycia. Roman rule brought it new life, until the earthquake of AD 141 dealt it a heavy blow. Yet Limyra endured, and in the Byzantine period it continued to exist as a bishopric.
structure-1: You are now at the Pericles Heroon, Limyra's famous tomb monument on the acropolis. It was built for the Lycian king Pericles, and it takes the form of a temple: a heroon adorned with caryatids. Here a king was honoured almost like a hero.
structure-3: Now look closely at the Kaineus Relief. Carved here at Limyra, it depicts Kaineus, a hero of mythology, caught in stone.
structure-4: Here stands the Monument of Gaius Caesar, raised at Limyra in memory of Gaius Caesar, the heir of Augustus. Pause for a moment: the heir to an emperor is remembered in this place.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Roman Theatre and the Rock-cut Tombs.
facts: Did you know? The Kaineus relief here is the most famous ancient depiction of the hero Kaineus, who was pinned into the ground with spears. Limyra was the capital of the Lycian king Pericles, and more than four hundred tombs are ranged on the cliff above it. And one more story: Gaius Caesar, Augustus' grandson and heir, died here, and the reliefs of the cenotaph raised for him were found in the city.
outro: This brings our journey through Limyra Ancient City to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Kings and heirs left their mark here; let it stay whole for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
